scenes.line1: How do you keep scripts safe in prod?
scenes.say: How do you make sure your script doesn't take down production? Let's break down what safe scripting really means.

scenes.label: Idempotent
scenes.sub: Only make changes if needed—never twice.
scenes.say: First, scripts should be idempotent. That means they only make changes if something actually needs fixing, not every time they run.

scenes.title: Dry-run & Logging
scenes.say: Add a dry-run flag so you can see what the script would do, before it does anything. And always log actions to a file and to the screen, with timestamps.

rows.b: Use env or vault, never in code

scenes.say: Harden your scripts: use strict error handling, never hard-code secrets, get every change reviewed in Git, and always run a linter like shellcheck to catch bugs early.

scenes.question: What's a common prod script mistake?
scenes.right: Skipping review lets bugs and risky changes go live. Always use pull requests.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: skipping code review to move fast. That lets risky changes slip through. Always use pull requests, even for scripts.
